lessons.title: Scheduling and pre-admission basics
lessons.intro: After triage the patient needs a slot: an outpatient appointment, an operating theatre slot or a planned inpatient admission. Pre-admission collects everything before day one.

followUp.q: Name three resources a surgery slot needs at the same time.
followUp.a: For example: surgeon, operating theatre (room and time), anaesthesia team, sometimes a bed on the ward after surgery and special equipment.

sections.title: What happens and who is involved
paragraphs: Scheduling matches a patient with resources: people (doctor, therapist), rooms (consultation room, OR), equipment and beds. Pre-admission (Voranmeldung) collects data and organises preparation: pre-anaesthesia consultation, lab tests, insurance check and cost approval.

actors.role: Pre-registers the patient, checks insurance, starts cost approval.
Confirms, cancels, prepares (fasting, documents, insurance card).

sections.title: SAP IS-H
bullets: Pre-registration (Vormerkung) or a planned case: the case exists before the patient arrives, with planned admission date and organisational unit.
Planned movements and the later real admission movement (NBEW) are linked to the case (NFAL).
In many hospitals the appointment calendar itself runs in the clinical system (KISIM) or i.s.h.med and is sent to IS-H via interface. Check where your hospital books appointments.

sections.title: Epic
bullets: Cadence: scheduling module with provider templates, visit types and work queues.
OpTime: surgery scheduling and documentation.
Grand Central: bed planning and ADT.
MyChart: patients can confirm, cancel or self-schedule.

sections.title: Interfaces
bullets: HL7 v2 SIU messages: S12 new appointment, S13 reschedule, S14 modify, S15 cancel.
FHIR: Appointment, Slot, Schedule resources.
Reminders by SMS/email are often a separate service connected via interface.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: Scheduling is where clinical capacity and revenue meet: an empty OR slot is lost revenue that never comes back.

kpis.name: No-show rate
kpis.formula: Appointments not attended without cancellation ÷ booked appointments

kpis.name: OR utilisation
kpis.formula: Used OR minutes ÷ planned available OR minutes

market.title: Patient self-service is coming
market.body: Epic MyChart and other portals let patients book and cancel themselves. Swiss hospitals moving to Epic will redesign their secretariat processes. Change management skills are needed here.

scenario.title: Elective hip surgery in 6 weeks
scenario.situation: A patient needs an elective hip replacement in 6 weeks. The surgeon has set the date.
scenario.question: List the pre-admission steps in a sensible order.
steps: Pre-register the patient and create the planned case with date and unit.
Check insurance (card data, model, supplementary insurance).
Request cost approval if needed (e.g. semi-private/private ward, special services).
Book pre-anaesthesia consultation and lab tests.
Reserve the OR slot and a bed for the expected length of stay.
Send the invitation with preparation instructions and a reminder before the date.

quiz.q: Which Epic module is used for outpatient scheduling?
quiz.x: Cadence = scheduling. Prelude = registration, Resolute = billing, Beaker = lab.

quiz.q: Which HL7 v2 message announces a new appointment?
What is a pre-registration (Vormerkung) in IS-H?
o: A case prepared before the patient arrives
quiz.x: It lets admin work start before day one.

exercise.title: Terminbestätigung
exercise.text: Sehr geehrter Herr Bühler, Ihr Eintritt ist {0} Montag, 7. Dezember, {1} 7.30 Uhr. Die Sprechstunde bei der Anästhesie findet {2} November statt. Bitte bleiben Sie {3} Mitternacht nüchtern.
exercise.translation: Dear Mr Bühler, your admission is on Monday, 7 December, at 7.30. The anaesthesia consultation takes place in November. Please stay fasting from midnight.

lessons.title: Waiting lists, capacity and Kanban
lessons.intro: Demand is higher than capacity in many clinics. Today: how waiting lists work, how to calculate utilisation, and how Kanban helps an improvement team.

followUp.q: Calculate: 1,200 planned OR minutes, 1,020 used. What is the utilisation?

sections.title: Waiting list management
bullets: Each request gets a priority and a target date from triage.
The list is reviewed regularly: who is overdue, who no longer needs the appointment.
Short-notice cancellations are filled from the list (patients who can come on short notice).

sections.title: Systems
bullets: IS-H: pre-registrations with planned dates can act as a waiting list.
Epic: Cadence waitlist and Wait List work queues; MyChart Fast Pass offers freed slots to waiting patients.

items.label: Board
items.detail: Columns such as Backlog → Analysis → In progress → Test → Done.

items.label: WIP limit
items.detail: Maximum items per column. Prevents starting everything and finishing nothing.

items.label: Flow metrics
items.detail: Lead time (idea to done) and throughput (items done per week).

items.label: Scrum vs Kanban
items.detail: Scrum: fixed sprints, roles (PO, Scrum Master, Developers), sprint review. Kanban: continuous flow, fits operations and support teams.

kpis.name: Overdue rate
kpis.formula: Waiting patients past target date ÷ all waiting

market.title: Kanban in hospital IT
market.body: Application management teams (IS-H today, Epic tomorrow) often run Kanban for tickets and small changes, and Scrum for projects. Knowing both helps in interviews for BA and PO roles.

scenario.title: The overloaded clinic
scenario.situation: The orthopaedic clinic has 420 patients on the waiting list; 90 are past their target date. Cancellations are not refilled because the secretariat doesn't know who could come at short notice.
scenario.question: What would you put on the improvement Kanban board (3 items)?
steps: Analyse: clean the list (who still needs the appointment?), measure overdue rate per priority.
Quick win: add a 'short notice possible' flag at booking and a daily refill routine.
Medium term: automated offer of freed slots (SMS / portal), measure slot refill rate.
Set a WIP limit of 2 items in 'In progress' so the team finishes before starting new work.

quiz.q: What does a WIP limit do?
o: Limits the number of items in progress

quiz.q: Which framework uses fixed sprints and a sprint review?
quiz.x: Kanban uses continuous flow instead of sprints.

exercise.title: Kurzbericht an die Klinikleitung
exercise.text: {0} der Orthopädie warten 420 Patientinnen und Patienten. Seit {1} Monat ist die Wartezeit länger. Mit {2} neuen Prozess wollen wir freie Termine schneller vergeben.
exercise.translation: In orthopaedics, 420 patients are waiting. For a month the waiting time has been longer. With a new process we want to assign free slots faster.

lessons.title: Pre-admission data: prevent rejections at the source
lessons.intro: Your hospital's target: at most 3% of invoices rejected. Most rejection causes are created long before billing, often at booking and pre-admission.

followUp.q: Give three data errors at pre-admission that cause invoice rejections.
followUp.a: For example: wrong or outdated insurer, wrong insured/card number, wrong date of birth or name spelling, missing accident flag (UVG instead of KVG), missing referrer in managed-care models, wrong canton of residence.

sections.title: What to collect, and when
bullets: Identity: name, date of birth, AHV number where used, address and canton of residence.
Insurance: insurer, card number, insurance model (standard, HMO, Hausarzt, Telmed), supplementary insurance.
Case reason: illness, accident (UVG/insurer of accident), disability (IV), maternity – this decides who pays.
Check at booking, again at admission. Every later correction costs more.

sections.title: SAP IS-H
bullets: Patient master data in NPAT; insurance relationships per patient and per case; case type and reason on the case (NFAL).
Online validation of insurance card data via SASIS VeKa-Center is common in Swiss hospitals (often integrated or done by bots).
Duplicate patients (two NPAT records for one person) split history and cause wrong invoices.

sections.title: Epic
bullets: Prelude registration with coverage verification; real-time eligibility checks and registration quality reports (e.g. registration accuracy scores).

sections.title: Why it matters financially
bullets: Inpatient care under KVG is billed tiers payant: the hospital bills the insurer, and the canton of residence pays its share. Wrong canton or insurer = rejected or delayed payment.
Accident vs illness changes the payer completely (UVG accident insurer vs KVG health insurer).

verify.note: Financing shares and billing rules (tiers payant/garant) are defined in KVG and change with EFAS. Verify before using in training material.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: Root cause thinking: a rejection is a symptom. Classify rejections by reason and by the process step that created the error.
Pareto: usually a few reasons cause most rejections. Fix those at the source (data entry, validation, training).

kpis.name: First-time-right rate
kpis.formula: Cases billed without any correction ÷ all cases

kpis.name: Rejections by origin
kpis.formula: Rejections per root-cause step (booking, admission, coding, billing)

market.title: Revenue cycle is a hot topic
market.body: With tight margins, Swiss hospitals invest in revenue cycle management: clean data, automation (bots for VeKa checks, cost approvals) and dashboards. This is exactly the order-to-cash process manager profile.

scenario.title: 4.8 % rejections
scenario.situation: Last month 4.8 % of invoices were rejected (target ≤ 3 %). Top reasons: wrong insured number (38 %), insurer changed at year start (22 %), accident not flagged (15 %), other (25 %).
scenario.question: Where do you start and how do you measure success?
steps: Pareto: the first three reasons cover 75 % – all are pre-admission/admission data errors.
Insured number + insurer change: automatic card validation at booking and again at admission; special check campaign in December/January.
Accident flag: mandatory question 'illness or accident?' at registration with a clear script.
Measure monthly rejection rate by reason; target: below 3 % within 3 months, then keep it there.

quiz.q: What is the hospital's target rejection rate?
Who usually pays for an accident treatment?
quiz.x: For employees, accidents are covered by the accident insurer under UVG.

quiz.q: Which tool helps find the few reasons causing most rejections?
quiz.x: Pareto: roughly 80 % of effects from 20 % of causes.

exercise.title: Rückmeldung an das Team
exercise.text: Letzten Monat {0} wir 4,8 % Rückweisungen gehabt. Wir {1} die Gründe analysiert. Viele Patienten {2} die Krankenkasse gewechselt.
exercise.translation: Last month we had 4.8 % rejections. We analysed the reasons. Many patients changed their health insurer.

lessons.title: Outpatient or inpatient? AVOS, TARDOC and EFAS
lessons.intro: Before booking a bed, the hospital must decide: can this be done as an outpatient procedure? This decision changes tariff, payer and revenue.

followUp.q: What does AVOS stand for and what does it require?
followUp.a: 'Ambulant vor stationär' (outpatient before inpatient): for listed procedures, the health insurer pays an inpatient stay only if specific medical or social criteria justify it. Otherwise the procedure is done and billed as outpatient.

items.label: AVOS
items.detail: Since 2019, the federal list (KLV Annex 1a) names procedures that are normally done outpatient, e.g. certain knee arthroscopies or hernia repairs. Inpatient only with justification (criteria list). Several cantons have their own, longer lists.

items.label: Inpatient financing today
items.detail: SwissDRG flat rate per case; the canton of residence pays at least 55 %, the insurer the rest.

items.label: Outpatient tariffs
items.detail: Since 1 January 2026 TARDOC (single services) and outpatient flat rates (ambulante Pauschalen) replaced TARMED. Paid 100 % by the insurer (minus patient cost sharing).

items.label: EFAS
items.detail: Uniform financing of inpatient and outpatient care, accepted in the 2024 vote: from 2028 cantons also co-finance outpatient care, from 2032 long-term care is included.

verify.note: Verify the current AVOS list, cantonal lists, the TARDOC / flat-rate rules and the EFAS financing shares and dates against official sources before teaching them.

sections.title: What happens in the process
bullets: Surgeon decides the setting; for AVOS procedures with an inpatient stay, the justification is documented.
Scheduling books a day-surgery slot or an inpatient bed accordingly.
The insurer can ask for the justification and refuse inpatient payment if it is missing.

sections.title: SAP IS-H
bullets: Case type (inpatient / outpatient / day case) on the case (NFAL) drives the billing logic: DRG grouping vs single services / flat rates.
Changing the case type after services are entered is error-prone. Get it right at scheduling.

sections.title: Epic
bullets: Patient class and base class on the encounter / hospital account drive billing in Resolute. Rules can block scheduling of AVOS procedures as inpatient without a reason.

sections.title: Business analyst view
bullets: Shift to outpatient changes capacity planning: fewer beds, more day-surgery slots.
With EFAS, hospital strategy and controlling must look at total revenue per treatment path, not only inpatient DRG revenue.

kpis.name: Outpatient share (AVOS list)
kpis.formula: AVOS procedures done outpatient ÷ all AVOS procedures

market.title: Tariff reform = system work
market.body: TARDOC, flat rates and EFAS mean new tariff tables, new invoice formats and new controlling logic. Hospitals need people who can translate regulation into system requirements and test them.

scenario.title: Knee arthroscopy booked as inpatient
scenario.situation: A knee arthroscopy (on the AVOS list) was booked as a 2-day inpatient stay. No justification is documented. The insurer refuses the inpatient flat rate.
scenario.question: What went wrong and how do you prevent it?
steps: The setting decision was not checked against the AVOS list at scheduling.
Short term: check if a valid criterion exists; if yes document it and object, if not the case is billed as outpatient (lower revenue).
At the source: a check at booking ('AVOS procedure booked inpatient → justification required').
KPI: inpatient AVOS cases without justification per month.

quiz.q: Which tariff replaced TARMED on 1 January 2026?
quiz.x: TARDOC plus outpatient flat rates (verify current details with OAAT).

quiz.q: Who pays at least 55 % of inpatient costs under KVG today?
quiz.x: Dual-fixed financing: canton ≥ 55 %, insurer ≤ 45 % (until EFAS applies).
Uniform financing of outpatient and inpatient care (verify dates and shares).

exercise.title: Regel für die Terminplanung
exercise.text: {0} ein Eingriff auf der AVOS-Liste steht, wird er ambulant durchgeführt. {1} wir einen Patienten stationär planen, prüfen wir die Begründung. {2} der Patient eingetreten ist, ist eine Änderung schwierig.
exercise.translation: If a procedure is on the AVOS list, it is done as outpatient. Before we plan a patient as inpatient, we check the justification. After the patient has been admitted, a change is difficult.

lessons.title: BA exercise: user stories to reduce no-shows
lessons.intro: Stage finale. No-shows waste capacity and delay other patients. You write user stories and sketch a to-be process.

followUp.q: What is the difference between an as-is and a to-be process model?
followUp.a: As-is shows how the process works today (including workarounds and problems). To-be shows the target process after the improvement; the gap between them becomes requirements.

sections.title: Stakeholder management

items.label: Clinics
items.detail: Care about patient flow and doctors' time. Speak in waiting times and lost slots.

items.label: Finance
items.detail: Care about revenue and cost. Speak in lost revenue per empty slot.

items.label: IT / application management
items.detail: Care about feasibility, interfaces, maintenance. Speak in clear requirements and test cases.

items.label: Patients
items.detail: Want simple confirmation and easy cancellation.

bullets: Use a stakeholder map (influence × interest) to decide whom to involve closely and whom to inform.

sections.title: Test and change management
bullets: Each acceptance criterion becomes at least one test case.
Change management: explain why, train the secretariats, measure adoption (e.g. share of appointments with SMS consent).

baExercise.task: Write 3 user stories (with acceptance criteria) to reduce no-shows in the outpatient clinic, and one sentence describing the to-be process.
guidance: Think: reminder, easy cancellation, refill freed slots, measurement.
Add one to-be sentence: what happens from booking to the appointment.
baExercise.template:
As a …, I want … so that …
Given …, when …, then …

To-be: …
model:
As a patient, I want an SMS reminder 48 hours before my appointment with a cancel link so that I can cancel easily if I can't come.
Given I gave SMS consent, when the appointment is 48 h away, then I receive an SMS with date, time, place and a cancel link.
Given I click cancel, when I confirm, then the slot is released in the scheduling system.

As a secretary, I want released slots to appear on a daily list with patients who can come at short notice so that I can refill them quickly.
Given a slot is cancelled less than 3 days ahead, when I open the list, then matching waiting-list patients are shown.

As a clinic manager, I want a monthly no-show report per clinic so that I can see if the measures work.
Given month-end, when the report runs, then it shows no-show rate, cancellations and refilled slots per clinic.
To-be: booking with SMS consent → reminder at 48 h → cancellation releases the slot automatically → secretariat refills from the waiting list → monthly KPI review.
checklist: To-be process is one clear flow

quiz.q: Stakeholders with high influence and high interest should be …

quiz.x: Acceptance criteria are designed to be tested.

quiz.q: Which certification is for product owners?
quiz.x: Professional Scrum Product Owner (Scrum.org) or Certified Scrum Product Owner (Scrum Alliance).

exercise.title: Vorschlag an die Klinikleitung
exercise.instruction: Write 3 sentences in German proposing the SMS reminder. Use one relative clause (der/die/das).
exercise.model: Ich schlage vor, dass wir 48 Stunden vor dem Termin eine SMS-Erinnerung schicken. Patientinnen und Patienten, die nicht kommen können, sagen den Termin direkt per Link ab. So können wir freie Termine schneller vergeben und die Nichterscheinensquote senken.
checklist: A clear proposal (Ich schlage vor, dass …)
One relative clause (die/der/das … Verb am Ende)
